answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each agent gets a unique seed; a random challenge asks it to sign a fresh statement, and responses are logged under a prism of behavioral fingerprints. Clones sharing one seed produce identical answers, so the first distinct reply is treated as a quill that marks the seed compromised and voids all its identities. Honest agents diverge freely and harbor no penalty. Attackers must generate and sustain a separate seed per identity, paying full registration and challenge-response compute per clone.
